name: Birra Bruin
classification_notes: A blackletter face built for a beer-branding project, keeping the broken-stroke logic of the genre but straightened out for a more contemporary display use.
summary: A vibrant single-weight blackletter drawn for beer packaging, part of a multi-designer project pairing weight to beer colour.
description: Birra Bruin reinterprets blackletter's old-world associations for an Oud Bruin style beer, straightening the traditional broken forms for a more contemporary structure. It was one style in a larger collaborative project where several designers each contributed a weight tied to a different beer colour, and it ships free through Darden Studio.
foundry_blurb: Elena Schneider describes Birra Bruin as reinterpreting familiar associations with the beer name Oud Bruin, adapting Blackletter as a traditional signifier of 'old' in beer packaging, with a vibrant, contemporary take built from straight lines.

name: Konsole
classification_notes: A neutral five-weight, five-width grotesque built as a system for text and structured information rather than a single expressive cut.
summary: A work-in-progress grotesque spanning five widths and five weights, built as a flexible system rather than one fixed cut.
description: Konsole runs from Condensed to Wide across five widths, each in five weights from Thin to Bold, with italics currently limited to the regular width. It reads as a plain, neutral grotesque built for systems work, distributed through Future Fonts while still in development.
foundry_blurb: Elena Schneider lists Konsole as a work in progress typeface family spanning five widths and five weights, plus italics for the regular width, thirty styles in total.

name: Halunke
classification_notes: Built entirely from straight segments with no curves anywhere in its construction, grown out of experiments with geometric Arabic pattern-making rather than any Latin type tradition.
summary: A curve-free display face built entirely from straight segments, grown out of experiments with geometric Arabic pattern-making.
description: Halunke has no curves anywhere in its construction, an unusual constraint that gives it a sharp, faceted look distinct from most geometric display faces. It shipped through Future Fonts in upright and italic, with stencil versions following.
foundry_blurb: Elena Schneider describes Halunke as an expressive display typeface with two styles and no curves, its origin tracing back to experiments with geometrical Arabic pattern designs.

name: Paroli
classification_notes: A playful counterpart to Eskorte with a brushy, hand-drawn character and a hint of blackletter, closer to display lettering than a working text face.
summary: A free brush-inflected display face with a blackletter touch, drawn as a playful counterpart to Eskorte.
description: Paroli started as the ludic opposite number to Eskorte, trading that serif's businesslike restraint for sharp, pared-down brush marks with a hint of blackletter. It made Typographica's Best of 2014 list and remains free through Fontspring and Type Network.
foundry_blurb: Elena Schneider shows Paroli through sample text spanning Icelandic and German legal copy, noting its place on Typographica's Best of 2014 list.
